text:
maya: Heads up — ran into a terraform lock/error during the regional AZ split apply for us-west-2. GPU pool module applied in 2 of 3 AZs and then CI failed with a lock contention.

maya: Logs: ```Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock for the Workspace: resource temporarily unavailable
  on main.tf line 12, in module \"gpupool\":
  12: module \"gpupool\" { ... }

Terraform will automatically release the state lock when the operation completes or is cancelled. You can also manually unlock using:
  terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID PATH```

sam: Ugh. Did the gitops pipeline fire parallel applies for each AZ workspace? I thought we serialized by region.

maya: It did not — our recent change split the module into az-scoped child modules and the pipeline kicked a per-az run concurrently. That made multiple terraform processes hitting the same backend key.

leo: Was the backend key per-workspace or global? If workspace scoping wasn't set correctly we could get collisions.

maya: Backend is remote S3+Dynamo with workspace=false (we rely on one state per cluster). Splitting modules without new workspaces caused the conflict.

tessa: Quick options:
- force-unlock the current lock then run a single apply in a queued job
- or use per-az workspaces and keep parallelism but different state keys
- or change GitOps to serialize region/cluster applies (preferred short term)

sam: I'm +1 on serializing the GitOps step for this rollout. We should avoid force-unlock unless we confirm the other apply is dead.

deploy-bot: CI: deploy job #4421 for repo infra/gpu-pools failed: lock_acquire_error. Queue position: 3.

leo: Another snag: KMS alias resource failed on one AZ with "already exists" during reapply. Looks like provider aliasing change caused duplicate alias creation when the partial apply rolled back.

maya: Right — the module change moved KMS alias creation into a per-az child module but the alias name is global. So when AZ-B applied it tried to create the same alias while AZ-A had already created it earlier. The provider semantics + partial state left us inconsistent.

tessa: Suggested fix list:
1) Immediately: pause per-az parallel runs, run a single reconciler apply (sam/leo to coordinate), and do not force-unlock unless confirmed.
2) Short-term code patch: make KMS alias resource conditional (only create when var.primary_az == var.az) or import existing alias if created.
3) Medium: move to workspace-per-az or update backend key naming to include az suffix so each az has its own state file.
4) Long: GitOps pipeline change to produce a per-region queue with concurrency=1 for infra changes that touch shared global resources.

sam: I'll coordinate the single apply. Leo, can you run `terraform state list | grep aws_kms_alias` to see where it thinks the alias lives and whether it has been recorded?

leo: On it. Output: ```aws_kms_alias.primary_alias
module.gpupool.module.kms.aws_kms_alias.primary_alias
```

leo: So state thinks alias exists under the module path from earlier apply. That's why a second create fails. We can import the resource in the AZ-specific module path rather than create.

maya: Good. Procedure for import:
- run `terraform import module.gpupool.module.kms.aws_kms_alias.primary_alias alias/your-alias` in the target workspace (or temp single-run)
- replan; ensure no create is attempted

tessa: Also recommend adding a guard in the module: `create_kms_alias = lookup(var, \"create_kms_alias\", true) && var.anchor == \"primary\"` so non-primary AZs skip. Minimal change.

sam: I'll queue a manual gate: pause the automated rollouts, mark the PR as manual apply, and tag oncall. Maya, can you prepare the apply command and ensure we set `-parallelism=10` and `-lock-timeout=300s`?

maya: Yes — will run `terraform apply -var 'region=us-west-2' -var 'anchor_az=us-west-2a' -parallelism=10` from the infra-admin bastion. I will not force-unlock unless infra-ci confirms no active operations.

infra-ci: Note: updated pipeline plugin to support queued infra runs. We'll enable it after the hotfix.

leo: After apply, we should create a lightweight migration guide in the repo explaining the state key naming implications for module splits. This bite-sized doc will prevent similar surprises.

maya: Agreed. Also adding a CI lint rule to fail if module split PRs don't include a state-plan: how will the change affect backend keys/workspaces.

tessa: OK plan settled. Sam will orchestrate the single apply, Maya runs it, Leo will import KMS alias if needed, I'll PR the conditional guard, infra-ci will flip queue mode after.

sam: Oncall tagged: @leo @maya @tessa — watch channel during apply.

maya: Running apply now — will post progress.

maya: Apply finished: success. No new alias creates, state reconciled. Rolling out rest of AZs one-at-a-time. :party_parrot:

sam: Nice. Follow-up action items: update GitOps pipeline to queue per-cluster infra changes, add state-change checklist to PR template, and add a test case for module split in staging. I'll open issues for each.

tessa: I'll send the PR for the KMS guard and a tiny doc for exporters.

deploy-bot: CI: job #4421 re-run queued -> success.

maya: Thanks everyone — closing this thread after we merge the guard and pipeline queue.
